papers.abstract: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.

analysis.key_results: 在7个模拟环境和4个真实机器人任务中，物体预测误差从15.20降至7.00，动作成功率从33.73%提升至72.96%；消融实验表明甚至可用单条测试交互轨迹高效推断环境隐变量。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出 T2-Z 方法，为机器人世界模型引入可学习的环境隐变量，通过训练和测试时的交替优化，实现无需监督的环境因素结构化捕获和快速适配。
analysis.method: T2-Z 在训练中交替执行世界模型优化阶段和环境隐变量优化阶段；测试时冻结世界模型，仅从少量交互中优化新初始化的环境隐变量。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: T2-Z 通过测试时优化环境隐变量，使机器人世界模型能够适应不可见的环境因素，从而提升预测精度和操作成功率。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 该工作直接针对机器人世界模型（WAM）的核心能力，通过测试时优化环境隐变量提升世界模型对未知环境的泛化和预测能力，对 VLA/WAM 研究具有直接且重要的方法学价值。

papers.abstract: We introduce P$^{3}$-WAM, a unified world action model for egocentric dexterous manipulation that learns 3D perception, action-conditioned prediction, and goal-directed planning through three complementary modes: Perceive, which reconstructs articulated hand motion and camera trajectories from video; Predict, which generates visual futures under prescribed actions; and Plan, which jointly generates action trajectories and their anticipated visual consequences conditioned on an initial image, a language instruction, and an optional visual goal. Our model integrates a compact, structured 3D action representation into a pretrained video diffusion transformer through a mixture-of-transformers architecture with shared base weights, modality-specific adaptation, and bidirectional visual-action attention. Randomized modality visibility lets video and 3D actions serve as either conditioning context or prediction targets across the three modes. Experiments show that unified training improves all three capabilities over single-mode training, including gains in planning quality under a vision-language model evaluation. Through unified training, our model outperforms specialized baselines on 3D hand reconstruction and action-conditioned video prediction across four datasets, while producing goal-directed manipulation videos with stronger instruction adherence and action progression than video-generation baselines. Project Page: https://p3-wam.pages.dev/

analysis.key_results: 统一训练相比单模式训练改善感知、预测和规划能力；在四个数据集上3D手部重建和动作条件视频预测超越专用基线；规划生成的操纵视频在指令遵循和动作进展上优于视频生成基线。
analysis.main_contribution: 引入P³-WAM，将3D动作与视频预测统一在同一个世界动作模型中，支持感知、预测、规划三种互补模式，并通过统一训练提升每一模式性能。
analysis.method: 将紧凑的结构化3D动作表示集成到预训练视频扩散Transformer中，采用混合Transformer架构（共享基础权重、模态特定适配、双向视觉-动作注意力）以及随机模态可见性来实现跨模式训练。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出P³-WAM，一个统一的自我中心灵巧操作世界动作模型，通过感知、预测和规划三种模式联合学习3D感知、动作条件预测和基于语言目标的条件规划。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 本文直接面向世界动作模型（WAM）这一核心主题，将感知、预测与规划统一在同一框架内，对机器人灵巧操作和视觉-语言引导的动作生成具有直接且重要的研究价值。

papers.abstract: Generative simulation can automate robot environment construction, but physically valid environments are not necessarily useful for training. The challenge is to identify environments that address a policy's failures and supervision that helps it overcome them. We introduce CoDA, a framework in which a simulation data engine and an action policy co-evolve through a shared heterogeneous memory of environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress. The memory compiles validated diagnoses from a vision-language critic into generation programs that recreate difficulties and training programs that help the policy overcome them. We further propose Text2potential to convert these diagnoses into staged potentials for action-chunk value learning, providing dense supervision for policy updates while preserving the task's optimal policy under standard shaping assumptions. Measured learning progress guides further generation and program refinement. Across four manipulation task families, CoDA improves out-of-distribution success from 5.3% after supervised fine-tuning to 27.6%, exceeding the strongest closed-loop baseline by 9.5 percentage points with the same generation budget. On LIBERO-Pro, 15 rounds of generation and training raise success from 25% to 84% under position perturbations and from 1% to 76% under instruction perturbations.

analysis.key_results: 在四个操作任务族上，CoDA 将分布外成功率从监督微调后的 5.3% 提高到 27.6%，比最强闭环基线高出 9.5 个百分点；在 LIBERO-Pro 上，15 轮生成与训练后在位置扰动下成功率从 25% 提高到 84%，在指令扰动下从 1% 提高到 76%。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出 CoDA 框架，使仿真数据引擎与动作策略通过共享异构记忆协同进化，并引入 Text2potential 将诊断转化为阶段性势能以提供稠密监督。
analysis.method: CoDA 使用共享异构记忆存储环境构造、策略失败和学习进展，视觉-语言评论家验证诊断并生成重建困难环境和训练程序的生成程序；Text2potential 将诊断转化为动作块值学习的阶段性势能。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: CoDA 框架通过共享异构记忆使仿真数据引擎与动作策略协同进化，利用视觉-语言评论家的诊断生成针对性的环境和监督，从而提升机器人操作策略的泛化性能。

papers.abstract: Few-step autoregressive video generators enable streaming generation, yet they run every token through the final denoising step, regardless of how much refinement it needs. We find this uniform computation is often unnecessary: many tokens already closely match their eventual full-step outputs in the initial steps, while others require refinement until the end. We introduce Speculative Forcing, a framework that treats intermediate clean estimates as drafts and predicts when individual tokens can be safely accepted early. Once accepted, a token is frozen as its final output and undergoes no further denoising, while its cached keys and values remain available as context for the remaining tokens. We explore two alternative verifier designs: a training-free one based on similarity to clean content and stability across steps, and a learned one that reads the frozen generator's intermediate features to estimate each token's remaining gap to its full-step output. Across short-video, long-video, and world generation, Speculative Forcing preserves the quality of full-step sampling while substantially reducing computation. On LongLive, it matches the four-step generator with ~1.7 denoising steps per token, running over 1.5x faster at 41.7 and 37.8 fps. On Lingbot-World 2.0, where camera motion continually changes the visible content, it maintains quality with ~2.5 denoising steps per token and runs 1.35x faster at 24.5 fps.

analysis.key_results: 在LongLive上，用约1.7步/ token达到四步生成器的质量，速度提升1.5倍以上；在Lingbot-World 2.0上，用约2.5步/ token保持质量，速度提升1.35倍。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出Speculative Forcing，一种允许自回归视频生成器在中间去噪步骤提前接受并冻结token，从而减少冗余计算的方法。
analysis.method: 将中间干净估计作为草稿，预测token能否安全提前接受；接受后冻结token，保留其缓存键值供后续token使用；探索了基于相似性和稳定性的免训练验证器以及基于特征的可学习验证器。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出Speculative Forcing框架，通过将中间去噪结果作为草稿并预测哪些token可提前接受，从而在保持生成质量的同时显著减少自回归视频生成的计算量。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 该工作聚焦于高效视频生成中的推测性解码，不直接涉及VLA或WAM，但其中对世界生成（world generation）任务的验证表明其可降低自回归世界模型推理开销，对WAM的高效推理具有方法借鉴价值。

papers.abstract: How can robots autonomously collect the contact-rich experience needed to learn dexterous manipulation? We present DSP: Dexterity from supervised play, a framework in which a robot learns a play policy from minutes of human play through behavior cloning, then deploys it autonomously to collect hours of interaction data to train a world model. During inference, the same play policy then guides model-predictive control (MPC) by proposing candidate action sequences for evaluation under the learned world model. To accelerate inference, we also introduce a method for distilling a closed-loop, goal-conditioned policy through self-play within the learned world model. We evaluate this framework on underactuated pushing and any-to-any in-hand pose reorientation with a multifingered hand, in simulation and real world. In real world experiment, our method outperforms hindsight behavior cloning by 69.6% in success rate and achieves comparable success to reinforcement learning with 490 times less interaction data. These results demonstrate that supervised play can autonomously collect interaction data, guide model-based planning, and enable policy learning without any task-specific demonstrations or sim-to-real transfer.

analysis.key_results: 在真实世界实验中，该方法成功率比事后行为克隆高69.6%，并以少490倍的交互数据达到与强化学习相当的成功率。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出DSP框架，使机器人能通过监督式玩耍自主收集交互数据，训练世界模型，并利用玩耍策略指导模型预测控制，加速推理，且无需任务特定演示或仿真到真实迁移。
analysis.method: 行为克隆学习玩耍策略，使用该策略自主收集数据训练世界模型，在推理时由玩耍策略为模型预测控制（MPC）提出候选动作序列，并通过在世界模型中的自玩蒸馏出闭环目标条件策略。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出DSP框架，通过行为克隆学习玩耍策略，自主收集接触丰富的数据训练世界模型，并利用该策略引导模型预测控制，实现灵巧操作。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 本文核心涉及世界模型（World Model）与机器人操作学习，与WAM主题高度相关。它展示了世界模型在机器人操作规划与策略学习中的应用，并提出了高效推理方法。

papers.abstract: Multimodal deep search is moving from short queries to long-horizon investigations that continually acquire evidence. However, training such agents remains constrained by limited challenging training questions and insufficient process feedback. We introduce MMSearch-OPD, combining controllable data refinement with joint reinforcement learning (RL) and on-policy distillation (OPD). Our Refine pipeline performs targeted expansion of reasoning chains derived from existing simple multimodal questions. Parameterized transformations control search depth and cross-modal evidence requirements while reusing existing image--question pairs. For training, answer rewards and lightweight behavior penalties guide RL, while the reward gap modulates token-level teacher guidance on imperfect student trajectories. An exponentially decaying distillation coefficient reduces teacher dependence as training proceeds. Experiments show gains from data refinement and further improvements from joint training after SFT, indicating stronger long-horizon multimodal deep search capabilities.

analysis.key_results: 实验显示数据细化带来性能提升，联合训练在SFT基础上进一步改进，表明更强的长程多模态深度搜索能力。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出MMSearch-OPD框架，结合可控数据细化（Refine pipeline）与联合强化学习和在线蒸馏，提升长程多模态搜索智能体的训练效果。
analysis.method: Refine pipeline对简单多模态问题的推理链进行定向扩展，通过参数化变换控制搜索深度和跨模态证据要求；训练中使用答案奖励与轻量级行为惩罚引导强化学习，并利用奖励差距调节对不完美学生轨迹的教师指导，蒸馏系数随训练指数衰减。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出MMSearch-OPD框架，通过可控数据细化与联合强化学习和在线蒸馏训练长程多模态搜索智能体。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 该论文针对长程多模态搜索智能体的训练方法提出数据细化与联合训练策略，属于通用策略学习与数据生成，与机器人的视觉-语言-动作（VLA）或世界-行动模型（WAM）无直接相关性，但其数据扩展和强化学习蒸馏思路可能对机器人多模态策略训练有间接借鉴价值。

papers.abstract: In robotic manipulation, the same observation often admits multiple feasible actions. Generative policies such as diffusion and flow matching naturally capture such multimodal behaviors, yet which mode is executed is left to random sampling and cannot be actively controlled. We propose Mode-Oriented Source Shaping (MOSS), which turns mode selection into an explicit choice of where generation starts. We first reveal, both empirically and theoretically, that deterministic flow transport induces mode-dependent structure in the source space. Under ideal deterministic ODE transport, distinct behavioral modes have distinct source-space preimages, while practical approximation errors can blur their boundaries due to imbalanced data, limited model capacity, and few inference steps. Motivated by this source-space structure, MOSS constructs semantically aligned mode-specific Gaussian sources that encode mode identity in the initial noise. A modality-strength estimator predicts the local degree of multimodality, which adaptively controls the geometry of the mode-specific sources. It contracts them toward a shared Gaussian where behaviors are similar and separates them near behavioral branching points. During deployment, the desired behavior is selected at inference simply by sampling from the corresponding component. Across 6 simulated and 3 real-world manipulation tasks, MOSS steers to the target mode up to 100% of the time with high task success, recovers minority modes at over 90% guidance rate under a 10:90 imbalance dataset, and surpasses mode-conditioned flow policy by 43.3 points of guidance rate on real robots.

analysis.key_results: 在6个仿真和3个真机操作任务中，目标模式引导率高达100%且任务成功率高；在10:90不平衡数据下，少数模式引导率超过90%；在真机上比模式条件流策略的引导率高出43.3个百分点。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出Mode-Oriented Source Shaping (MOSS)，将流匹配策略中的模式选择显式化为生成起始位置的选择，并设计模态强度估计器自适应调整源分布几何结构。
analysis.method: 理论分析与实验揭示确定性流传输在源空间形成模态相关结构；构建语义对齐的模态特定高斯源；模态强度估计器预测局部多模态程度以收缩或分离源分布；推理时从对应分量采样实现目标模式引导。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 该论文提出MOSS方法，利用流匹配策略源空间中的模式结构，通过构造模态特定的高斯源来显式控制机器人操作中行为模式的选择。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 该论文直接针对机器人操作策略中的多模态动作生成问题，提出的MOSS方法属于机器人策略学习范畴，可视为对VLA策略中动作模式控制的重要改进，对提高机器人行为的可控性和数据不平衡鲁棒性具有直接价值。

papers.abstract: We introduce REKI, a 2.4B vision-language-action model (VLA) pretrained exclusively on public data that sets a new Pareto frontier between performance and model size: on LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin Clean2Rand and RoboCasa365, it is outperformed only by models about twice its size. REKI consists of a vision-language model (VLM) followed by a flow-matching action expert, and is pretrained on a curated mixture of public robot, egocentric human and vision-language data. Additionally, we endow it with a memory that gives the policy access to its recent past at negligible cost: a few register tokens in the action expert summarise the output of the VLM at each frame and persist in the expert's cache. This memory improves success in simulation and on real robots, and makes oscillations between poses about four times rarer. REKI uses a simple model design and training paradigm, and is optimised to be efficient at training and inference. We release the full code across data curation, training, inference and evaluation, deployment, and all pretrained and finetuned model weights: https://github.com/kyutai-labs/reki.

analysis.key_results: 在LIBERO-Plus、RoboTwin Clean2Rand和RoboCasa365上，仅被约两倍大小的模型超越；记忆机制提高仿真和真实机器人成功率，使姿态间振荡减少约四倍。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出REKI，一个2.4B的VLA模型，在LIBERO-Plus、RoboTwin Clean2Rand和RoboCasa365上建立了新的性能-模型尺寸帕累托前沿，并引入寄存器记忆机制以极低成本利用近期历史改善性能。

papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models present a promising paradigm for general-purpose robot manipulation, but closed-loop deployment is often limited by inference efficiency: at each timestep, high-resolution, often multi-view images are encoded into hundreds of visual tokens that dominate transformer computation and latency. Token compression via attention is a natural solution but is challenging for VLA control because (1) decision-critical tokens are determined by the task, not generic visual saliency, and (2) the token budget varies substantially across steps, so static metrics and budgets waste computation or discard control-critical tokens. We introduce FastVLA, a training-free, task-aware, and temporally adaptive visual token compression framework. At each step, FastVLA scores token importance via task-to-vision attention and adaptively sets the compression rate from the importance-distribution uniformity, measured by an inverse-Simpson metric with online sliding-window calibration. We evaluate FastVLA on OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, and CogACT across LIBERO and SIMPLER, and on a physical Franka Research 3 robot. In simulation, it reduces LLM-backbone FLOPs by 35-59\% and action latency by 9-32\% (a 1.09$\times$-1.46$\times$ speedup) while maintaining task success, achieving a comparable or better efficiency-performance trade-off than existing plug-and-play token compression/pruning/reuse baselines. On the real robot, it cuts end-to-end latency by 20\% (1.25$\times$ speedup) at comparable success. Code is available at https://github.com/jiuyixu25/FastVLA.

analysis.key_results: 在模拟中，LLM 骨干计算量减少 35-59%，动作延迟降低 9-32%（1.09×-1.46×加速）；在真实 Franka 机器人上，端到端延迟降低 20%（1.25×加速），成功率相当。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出 FastVLA，一个无需训练、任务感知且时间自适应的视觉令牌压缩框架，通过任务到视觉注意力动态调整压缩率，平衡推理效率与任务成功率。

papers.abstract: In minoritized (low-resource) language technologies, a common response to data sparsity is to aggregate text across multiple varieties and treat the combined data as a single corpus. However, mixed corpora of closely related indigenous variants can produce an artificial register that is accountable to no single speaker community, a structural failure we call variant fragmentation. This issue is acute for minoritized languages native to Mexico, such as Nawatl. Building on a 70,000-pair multi-variant foundation, we specialize an mT5-large checkpoint to Masewalkopa (nhn), the Nawatl variety spoken in Santa Ana Tlacotenco. We curate 2,665 parallel pairs, reserve all sentence-level data for evaluation, and incorporate 192 elder-transcribed target sentences via asymmetric backtranslation. A custom finite-state analyzer reduces unanalyzed surface forms from 82.0% to 19.9% and supplies functional syntax tags as plain-text prefixes, allowing the model to reuse existing subword embeddings rather than relying on frozen special tokens. The resulting LoRA-v9c-b model achieves 58.46 dev chrF++ and 58.20/57.90 directional test chrF++. Finally, CTranslate2 int8 quantization reduces CPU latency from 137.5 to 1.8-2.6 seconds per request, enabling cost-bounded Cloud Run deployment.

analysis.key_results: dev chrF++ 58.46，定向测试 chrF++ 58.20/57.90；未分析表面形式从 82.0% 降至 19.9%；CPU 延迟从 137.5 秒降至 1.8-2.6 秒。
analysis.main_contribution: 在 70,000 对多方言基础模型上，针对 Masewalkopa 这一 Nawatl 方言，利用 2,665 个平行句对和不对称回译进行专业化，并引入自定义有限状态分析器降低未分析表面形式比例，最终通过 CTranslate2 int8 量化将 CPU 延迟从 137.5 秒降到 1.8-2.6 秒，实现低成本部署。

analysis.one_sentence_summary: 通过单一方言专业化、数据增强和 int8 量化构建低资源语言 Nawatl 的机器翻译模型，大幅降低 CPU 推理延迟。

papers.abstract: Streaming vision-language models (VLMs) must continuously integrate information from the past while remaining responsive to current observations and user queries. Existing memory mechanisms typically compress, retrieve, or cache historical observations and reintroduce them into the input context, forcing historical memory and current observations to compete for limited context. We propose MaLoW, a streaming memory framework that instead internalizes historical context into evolving lightweight parameter updates. MaLoW uses a recurrent HyperNetwork to incrementally consolidate incoming video observations into fixed-size LoRA weights, allowing historical information to be carried forward without revisiting the full video stream. In doing so, MaLoW represents history as weights, while keeping the current observation as input. To support training, we further construct MaLoW-Instruct, a large-scale streaming video dataset containing 381K question-answer pairs over 56K videos. We conduct extensive experiments to demonstrate that MaLoW achieves strong performance on OVO-Bench, StreamingBench, and StreamArena. On the backward split of OVO-Bench, MaLoW outperforms prior memory approaches by 3.9% to 11.8% across different video backbones while incurring only modest latency overhead. Beyond streaming video understanding, MaLoW also generalizes to vision-language-action models, improving the action success rate on Simpler WidowX by 9.3%.

analysis.key_results: 在OVO-Bench、StreamingBench和StreamArena上表现强劲；OVO-Bench backward split上相比先前记忆方法提升3.9%-11.8%；在Simpler WidowX上动作成功率提升9.3%。

papers.abstract: World-model planners evaluate candidate trajectories by predicting their future consequences, implicitly relying on the plan-to-motion relationship learned during training. At deployment, a different downstream controller may execute the same planned trajectory differently, creating a planning-execution gap between the frozen model's imagined future and actual execution. A natural remedy is to replace the planned trajectory with its predicted or observed execution. However, we find that better execution fidelity does not necessarily yield better decisions: directly substituting predicted execution trajectories yields only a 0.048 PDMS improvement across 10 unseen controller configurations, far smaller than the gain from our proposed adaptation. This suggests a semantic mismatch between a planned trajectory, which serves as a reference for downstream control, and an executed trajectory, which already describes the resulting post-controller motion. We introduce ExecutionBridge, which infers controller-specific execution characteristics from planned-executed trajectory pairs and uses them to adapt the native ego latent rollout while keeping the original planned trajectory unchanged. The planner, world model, and reward head remain frozen. On NAVSIM, ExecutionBridge consistently improves planning across unseen controller configurations and multiple frozen world-model planners, with substantially larger gains in challenging driving scenes where execution mismatch more strongly affects candidate evaluation.

analysis.key_results: 在 NAVSIM 上，ExecutionBridge 在多个未见控制器配置和多个冻结世界模型规划器上一致提升规划性能；在具有挑战性的驾驶场景中收益更大。与直接替换预测执行轨迹仅获得 0.048 PDMS 改进相比，所提方法获得显著更高改进。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出 ExecutionBridge，利用控制器特定的执行特性适应冻结世界模型规划器的自我潜在状态滚动，在不修改规划器、世界模型和奖励头的情况下提高规划质量。

analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出 ExecutionBridge，通过从计划-执行轨迹对推断控制器特性来调整世界模型规划中的自我潜在状态滚动，以减小规划-执行差距并提升决策质量。

papers.abstract: Flow-based Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies are inherently stochastic: different noise seeds can produce action chunks of varying quality from the same observation. At test time, however, the policy typically commits to a single sample without an explicit estimate of its quality. In fine-grained manipulation, executing a suboptimal action can irreversibly disrupt task progress and lead to failure. To exploit policy stochasticity, we introduce a training-free two-axis trigger that uses two initial samples to measure within-chunk temporal variation and cross-sample variance, detecting the critical states. Once triggered, a JEPA-based latent world model ranks candidate action chunks by predicting action-conditioned future latent states and the corresponding changes in task progress. By operating in latent space, the verifier avoids pixel reconstruction and enables efficient and more accurate ranking. Across three real-world tasks, $\textit{i.e.,}$ pen insertion, pipetting, and apple placement), our method raises the average completion score from 50.8% to 65.5%, while adding 326 ms for sampling and verification per triggered decision on a single RTX 4090. Consistent gains are also observed in simulation, where the average success rate rises from 66.4% to 73.6% in the clean setting of RoboTwin 2.0, from 62.8% to 69.6% in its randomized setting, and from 96.9% to 97.6% on LIBERO.

papers.abstract: Learning from experience requires recovering reusable knowledge and determining when it applies to a new situation. We introduce OntoAct, a hypothesis-based neuro-symbolic framework built on ontological abstraction. OntoAct turns individual experiences into axioms over entity types, relations, and conditions, making their underlying patterns reusable across situations. A large language model (LLM) uses this world knowledge to propose hypotheses and actions, while a symbolic verifier assesses their supporting conditions against current observations. Verification identifies missing evidence, and new observations and intervention outcomes update hypothesis assessments and guide subsequent actions. We also introduce Tacit-FLE, a benchmark built on the Factorio Learning Environment (FLE) for diagnosing and repairing hidden faults in existing factories using inherited operational records. Its synthetic maintenance corpus distributes evidence across records, and an executed repair may leave the fault unresolved, requiring agents to reassess their diagnoses through interaction. Across Tacit-FLE, Mars, and ALFWorld, OntoAct achieves leading task performance with efficient interaction and inference.

papers.abstract: Many vision-language-action policies rely on action-labeled robot demonstrations and lack an explicit mechanism for predicting future visual states. These limitations hinder learning from action-free videos and can encourage overfitting to demonstration conditions, weakening generalization and robustness. We present TS-WAM, a lightweight Teacher-Student World-Action Model that addresses these challenges through self-supervised temporal learning and explicit future prediction. Its vlm-jepa framework learns from heterogeneous data, including robot demonstrations and action-free human videos, using an EMA target branch without requiring a separately trained external teacher. By coupling vlm-jepa with delta-lwm, TS-WAM learns to predict latent actions from the current observation and instruction and uses them to predict future visual features that guide action generation at inference. A unified end-to-end training architecture jointly optimizes temporal representation learning, visual dynamics, and robot control without a separate latent-action or world-model pretraining stage. The EMA target branch is removed at inference, keeping the deployed policy lightweight. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and SimplerEnv, together with real-world manipulation experiments on Franka Research 3 and RevoTron, demonstrate that TS-WAM achieves strong manipulation performance, generalization, and robustness.

papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies are typically trained with action prediction as the primary supervision signal, since robots ultimately execute actions. Auxiliary objectives such as latent-action (LA) and future-vision (FV) prediction are often added to improve policy learning, yet they compete with action prediction for the same training budget. We ask whether, under a fixed budget, allocating a substantial share of training samples to such objectives, rather than to further action prediction, can improve policy learning. We build a unified VLA framework that couples a two-stream multimodal diffusion transformer (MMDiT) with a sample-level router, which assigns each training sample to either action prediction or an auxiliary objective and thus makes supervision allocation explicit. Within this framework, we instantiate three LA targets based on LAPA and its DINO-feature variants, and three FV targets based on DINOv3, V-JEPA 2, and Wan2.2 representations. Across LIBERO, CALVIN, and four real-robot tasks, suitable LA and FV supervision outperforms action-only training under the same budget, even when action prediction receives no more than half of the training samples. FV generally outperforms LA, although the strongest LA target remains competitive on CALVIN. Diagnostic analyses suggest that DINO-based LA targets emphasize relative motion, whereas FV targets emphasize absolute position and task identity. We therefore argue that what robot policies learn to predict, and how training is allocated among these targets, should be treated as explicit design choices rather than defaulting to action-dominant training.

papers.abstract: Aggressive quantization of neural networks can expose activation functions as bottlenecks for efficient hardware acceleration. Implementing quantized activations as multi-threshold operations has been shown to be a promising optimization, allowing for efficient hardware implementation of few-bit activations. However, current implementations are limited to monotonically increasing functions, quantization schemes with one-dimensional (per-channel) granularity and a small set of predefined activation-quantizer combinations. We formalize the multi-threshold representation to extend it to non-monotonic functions and fine-granular parameters, i.e., multi-dimensional thresholds. For automated conversion of quantized function compositions into threshold representation, we propose a systematic approach via algebraic rules integrated into the ONNX-based compiler infrastructure. We experimentally validate our solution on a selection of monotonic and non-monotonic functions by extending the binary search based multi-threshold operator that is integrated into the FINN framework for end-to-end synthesis of custom-tailored FPGA accelerators. The cost of hardware support for non-monotonicity and fine-granularity is characterized in comparison to an alternative approach utilizing existing operators via graph-level decomposition. We compare our method to prior work as well as the approach taken by the hls4ml framework. As an outlook, we demonstrate the prospects of using the multi-threshold representation during the training of a neural network as a form of quantization aware training.

papers.abstract: Weight quantization below four bits shrinks memory and bandwidth at a perplexity that looks acceptable, but often at the cost of factual knowledge and task accuracy. Ternary weights have mostly been obtained by training from scratch or long fine-tuning. We introduce RoleQ, a quantization framework that places scales by the functional roles of Transformer units rather than by the layout of the weight matrix, as conventional formats do. Vectors that read from the residual stream take one scale per output unit; those that write to it, one per input unit. The rule is structural, needs no search, calibration or stored state, and holds on integer and ternary grids. In a rotated basis it matches a per-layer axis search at half the solver work, and at ternary it cuts perplexity by up to half against layout-based placement in two families at every size from 0.6B to 14B, where per-row scales leave MMLU at chance. Our lightweight post-training pipeline converts an existing checkpoint to 1.59 bits per weight in a few GPU-hours, a fraction of the cost of learned ternarization, and leads every post-training ternary method at matched or lower memory-resident bits on perplexity, zero-shot accuracy and MMLU, most widely on knowledge. A sparse second ternary plane placed by a per-unit Fisher saliency keeps the matmul multiplication-free and recovers what ternary loses first: at 8B, a fraction of a bit returns about half the MMLU that conversion costs, well ahead of random or Hessian-based placement at equal bits.

analysis.key_results: 在0.6B到14B模型上，三值量化困惑度最高降低一半；MMLU上领先所有后训练三值方法；8B模型上增加少量比特可恢复约一半因转换损失的MMLU。
analysis.main_contribution: 引入按功能角色而非权重矩阵布局放置量化尺度的三值量化框架RoleQ，无需搜索、校准或存储状态，显著提升低比特下的困惑度和知识准确性。
analysis.method: 根据Transformer单元读/写残差流的功能角色分别按输出单元或输入单元放置尺度，应用于整数和三值网格，并利用稀疏第二三值平面结合Fisher显著性进行补偿。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: RoleQ提出一种按Transformer单元功能角色放置量化尺度的后训练三值量化框架，以极低成本将语言模型压缩至1.59比特并保持知识能力。

papers.abstract: Scaling robot manipulation models requires large amounts of interaction data, yet collecting diverse real-robot experience remains costly. Human manipulation videos, in contrast, provide abundant and diverse task experience that could potentially benefit robot learning. However, differences in morphology, action spaces, and control mechanisms make human motions unsuitable as direct supervision for robot actions, raising a scientific question: what knowledge in human videos should be transferred across embodiments to robot manipulation? To address this question, we analyze subtask transfer through the lens of causal beams, focusing on which contextual conditions and interaction dependencies should be retained to support local task effects. Based on this perspective, we propose Causal-Beam-Guided Subtask Transfer (CBST). CBST learns manipulation-related representations from human videos and grounds them in task-level semantic variables using robot demonstrations. Within a predefined manipulation model, causal-beam constraints guide contextual information selection by requiring retained assignments to sustain local mechanism outputs while preserving nontrivial responsiveness to retained inputs. The selected semantic information conditions a world-action model, allowing the robot to generate actions from its own observations without requiring human-robot motion correspondence. Experiments on robot manipulation benchmarks show improvements in task success over the corresponding world-action model baselines.

papers.abstract: We study how vision-language models (VLMs) can learn to think and actively explore in 3D space. Instead of providing multi-view images, videos, or 3D representations to the model, we preserve the native visual encoding of VLMs, i.e., a single image, one at a time, just like humans, and treat the 3D representation only as an environment with which the model can interact through actions (e.g., move left) and observations (rendered images). Each rollout begins from an initial first-person view and a visual question. The model can then iteratively reason, navigate, and reorient its viewpoint before committing to a final answer. Following an initial trajectory-supervised finetuning, we apply reinforcement learning (RL) with rewards driven primarily by final-answer correctness. Crucially, RL provides no direct supervision over which viewpoints the model should visit or which exploration actions it should take. Instead, the model must learn an effective exploration policy solely from the extent to which its interactions improve performance. Across six 3D benchmarks, our model ACT3D achieves an average accuracy of 53.2% that improves its base Qwen model by 22.0% and surpasses proprietary Gemini 3.6 Flash. ACT3D also outperforms existing open-source 3D methods while using 50-70% fewer input frames, and generalizes to unseen domains with an average improvement of 5.9% over its supervised initialization. Further analysis reveals adaptive, question-conditioned exploration. Performance gains over the base model increase from 0.6% on questions answerable from the initial view to 16.3% on those requiring extensive exploration. ACT3D searches for occluded targets, avoids unnecessary exploration, and acquires complementary viewpoints for spatial comparisons. These findings demonstrate that outcome-based RL enables VLMs not only to reason over visual evidence, but also to learn when and how to acquire it.

analysis.key_results: 在六个3D基准上平均准确率53.2%，比基础Qwen模型提升22.0%，超过闭源Gemini 3.6 Flash；比现有开源3D方法少用50-70%输入帧，并在未见领域平均提升5.9%。

papers.abstract: Fixed-function CNN accelerators make edge inference fast and energy-efficient, but they execute only networks that obey a precise numerical contract. On the MAX7800x family, this contract requires power-of-two, per-tensor, symmetric scales, 8-bit activations and biases, integer-only arithmetic, and one statically configured shift per layer. We present ShiftQAT, the quantization-aware training (QAT) flow we developed for this family, which produces networks satisfying the contract by construction. It is the default training path of ai8x-training, the family's open-source training toolchain. ShiftQAT resolves residual, concatenation, and weight-sharing dependencies so that activation scales propagate statically and each layer's requantization reduces to one offline-configured shift. It also trains weights and biases on a joint power-of-two grid that fits the 8-bit bias budget. Among the compared methods, only ShiftQAT satisfies all of the contract's scaling constraints, including signed 8-bit activation storage. Even so, on ImageNet it matches the W8A8 accuracy drop of less constrained QAT methods and stays within 2.9 percentage points of FP32 at W4A8. On MAX78002 silicon, ShiftQAT-trained MobileNetV2 and ResNet-18 classify ImageNet images in 14.6 and 8.4 ms at 5.1 and 2.8 mJ per inference.

analysis.key_results: 在ImageNet上，ShiftQAT与约束较少的QAT方法具有相同的W8A8精度下降，在W4A8下与FP32相比精度差在2.9个百分点以内；在MAX78002硅片上，MobileNetV2和ResNet-18的ImageNet推理时间分别为14.6毫秒和8.4毫秒，能耗分别为5.1毫焦和2.8毫焦。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出ShiftQAT量化感知训练流程，能够为MAX7800x固定功能CNN加速器生成满足其严格数值契约（2的幂、每张量对称尺度、8位激活与偏置、整数运算、每层静态移位）的网络。
analysis.method: 通过静态解析残差、拼接和权重共享依赖，使激活尺度静态传播，每层重量化简化为离线配置的单次移位；在联合2的幂网格上训练权重与偏置，并作为ai8x-training的默认训练路径。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: ShiftQAT是一种为MAX7800x系列固定功能加速器设计的量化感知训练流程，通过强制满足硬件数值契约，在ImageNet上实现接近无约束QAT的精度和高效硅片推理。

papers.abstract: Reliable contact-rich manipulation requires detecting execution deviations early enough for corrective action. Yet most monitoring methods are reactive, identifying anomalies only after they become observable. Anticipating such anomalies is challenging because visual observations only partially reveal physical interaction, while planned actions describe intended motion rather than their actual physical consequences. We address this problem with MAIA, a multimodal framework for anomaly anticipation. Its vision-action-force world model learns nominal interaction dynamics and predicts the visual and force responses of planned actions, while a lightweight anomaly head predicts impending interaction anomalies. To enable systematic evaluation, we introduce CRIA, a real-world multimodal dataset of 2,852 trajectories spanning 18 contact-rich manipulation tasks, with frame-level annotations of anomaly onset and evolution. Experiments on both seen and novel tasks show that MAIA achieves more accurate anomaly discrimination than representative baselines while providing earlier warnings, with bACC scores of 0.765 and 0.710 and median anticipation lead times of 28.0 and 25.1 steps, respectively. Moreover, using these predictions for anomaly-aware action selection improves end-to-end task success from 52.6% to 61.5% without retraining the underlying manipulation policy. These results highlight the value of modeling future physical consequences for proactive anomaly anticipation.

analysis.key_results: 在已见和新任务上，MAIA的bACC分别为0.765和0.710，中位预测提前时间分别为28.0和25.1步；利用预测进行异常感知动作选择使端到端任务成功率从52.6%提高到61.5%（无需重新训练底层操作策略）。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出MAIA，一个用于接触丰富操作中异常预测的多模态框架，通过视觉-动作-力世界模型学习名义交互动力学并预测规划动作的视觉与力响应，结合轻量级异常头预测即将发生的交互异常；同时引入真实世界多模态数据集CRIA，包含18个接触丰富操作任务、2852条轨迹及帧级异常起始与演化标注。

papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) improves multimodal reasoning, but group-relative policy optimization broadcasts a single sequence-level advantage to every token of a response, although errors usually localize to a few decisive steps. Recent self-distilled variants refine credit with a teacher--student likelihood gap. However, this signal cannot tell whether it relies on the image or on a language shortcut, and is applied uniformly even when the teacher is uninformative. To address this, we propose Pairwise token contrast and Adaptive trajectory ConfidencE (PACE). Pairwise token contrast scores each response under four teacher views, crossing a correct or incorrect answer hint with the image present or removed, and compares the two hints for every token, which cancels shifts shared by both hints and reveals whether the token's support relies on the image. Adaptive trajectory confidence measures how well the teacher predicts each response given the correct hint and the image, normalizes this score within the batch, and uses it to set how far the token contrast redistributes credit within that response. PACE achieves the best average accuracy on three backbones and ranks first on all evaluated multimodal reasoning benchmarks with Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct. Experiments show that both components matter: replacing pairwise token contrast with a single-view signal underperforms our method, while adaptive trajectory confidence adds further improvement.

papers.abstract: Recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) enable automated preference labeling for robotic manipulation, yet their deployment remains impractical since each query incurs substantial inference cost, while VLMs frequently abstain on visually challenging comparisons. We propose SPEAR, a framework that transforms VLMs into efficient preference oracles via two synergistic mechanisms. First, we design distinguishability-aware query selection to reduce abstention rates by targeting only informative and distinguishable comparisons. Second, we deploy an adaptive reward transition that bootstraps exploration with VLM-synthesized guidance before preference-based refinement. Experiments on the manipulation benchmarks demonstrate that SPEAR achieves 88.9% average success, outperforming baselines by 23.3 percentage points, while significantly reducing abstention and wall-clock training time on contact-rich tasks. SPEAR learns three Mobile ALOHA manipulation tasks fully online on real hardware, demonstrating end-to-end real-world applicability. By addressing query efficiency and exploration challenges, SPEAR establishes VLMs as practical preference oracles for scalable robot learning without manual reward engineering.

analysis.key_results: 在操作基准上平均成功率达88.9%，比基线高23.3个百分点；显著降低弃权率和接触丰富任务的墙钟训练时间；在真实硬件上全在线学习三个Mobile ALOHA操作任务。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出SPEAR框架，通过区分感知查询选择和自适应奖励过渡，使视觉语言模型成为实用的机器人操作偏好预言机，无需人工奖励工程。
analysis.method: 区分感知查询选择减少VLM弃权；自适应奖励过渡先用VLM合成引导，再进行基于偏好的细化。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: SPEAR通过区分感知的查询选择和自适应奖励过渡，将视觉语言模型转化为高效的机器人操作偏好预言机，以降低推理成本和弃权率。
analysis.relation_to_vla_wam: 该工作直接利用视觉语言模型（VLM）为机器人操作策略提供偏好信号，属于视觉-语言-动作（VLA）学习范式，与本站主题高度相关。其核心贡献在于通过高效查询和奖励设计使VLM成为实用的偏好预言机，推动可扩展的机器人学习。

papers.abstract: Distilling vision-language features into 3D Gaussian Splatting yields a language map that can be queried with arbitrary text. In deployment, however, a small set of user-specified targets must be reliably located, which current distilled maps often miss, while open-vocabulary queryability for other words must remain intact. We propose a training-free, target-aware refinement of an already-distilled language map. Guided by a text-promptable segmenter, the visual embedding inside each detected target region is blended with the target text embedding, a convex combination whose coefficient sets the amount of injected prior, while non-target regions are left untouched. Injecting too much overwrites appearance cues and general queryability, so we seek, for each target, the smallest coefficient that still lets it win, and we obtain every coefficient in closed form, leaving no hyperparameters to tune. We further identify a failure mode of injection in language-goal localization. Text embeddings share a common component, and injecting them makes the standard cosine read-out query-agnostic, which a centering step in the read-out removes. Across three benchmarks, the refinement consistently improves open-vocabulary segmentation, roughly doubling the base mIoU on Replica, and localizes language goals more reliably than the base map. It also transfers as a plug-in to off-the-shelf field-based and object-level language maps and supports a real-world demonstration in which a legged robot navigates to natural-language goals. Project page and code: https://lab-of-ai-and-robotics.github.io/target-aware-langmap/

papers.abstract: Looped Transformers improve parameter efficiency by repeatedly applying the same Transformer layers. However, generating each token still involves sequential computation and repeated access to model weights, leading to high decoding latency. Recent pipelined self-speculative decoding methods reduce this delay by drafting tokens from early-loop predictions and asynchronously advancing tokens at different recurrent depths in the same batch, but they do not fully exploit early-loop features for longer lookahead and still spend computation verifying incorrect speculative branches. We introduce \method, a speculative decoding framework for looped transformers that enables earlier drafting of future tokens and assigns complementary roles to different recurrent depths. A lightweight lookahead drafter (LAD) predicts multiple future tokens with early-loop states, and deeper-loop feedback helps decide which draft branches to continue and which to pause, while the full-depth model makes the final token decisions. LoopAhead achieves up to 7.82x decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding while preserving the target model's output distribution.

analysis.key_results: 相对于自回归解码，LoopAhead 实现最高 7.82 倍解码加速，同时保持目标模型输出分布。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出 LoopAhead 推测解码框架，为循环 Transformer 引入轻量级前瞻起草器（LAD）与深层循环反馈机制，实现早期起草与分支裁剪，达成最高 7.82 倍解码加速且保持目标模型输出分布。
analysis.method: 轻量级前瞻起草器（LAD）使用浅层循环状态预测多个未来 token；深层循环反馈决定哪些推测分支继续或暂停；全深度模型做出最终 token 决策。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: LoopAhead 为循环 Transformer 提出一种推测解码框架，利用浅层循环状态提前起草多个未来 token，并通过深层反馈决定推测分支的继续或暂停，在保持输出分布的同时实现高达 7.82 倍的解码加速。

papers.abstract: While Assist-as-Needed (AAN) control aims to maximize user participation in robot-assisted training, existing methods relying solely on physical metrics cannot distinguish muscular inability from mental disengagement, leading to suboptimal interventions. To address this ambiguity, a Flow-theoretic multimodal AAN framework is proposed, fusing EEG-based mental engagement and sEMG-based physical engagement into an adaptive impedance control strategy. A four-quadrant fuzzy decision engine translates these dual physiological metrics into continuous control policies. This enables the upper-limb exoskeleton to inject feedforward assistance during intent-execution mismatch (e.g., motor output attenuation despite mental focus) and escalate guiding stiffness to penalize mental distraction. The framework was validated with healthy participants against a state-of-practice sEMG-only AAN baseline. Kinematically and mechanically, the proposed framework reduced robotic energy expenditure by 71.9\% while maintaining precise trajectory tracking, confirming it elicited greater voluntary human effort. Physiologically, the system increased the time spent in the neuroplasticity zone (Flow State Ratio) from 4.6% to 42.8%. These results validate that decoupling and jointly regulating mental and physical states enhances the selectivity of robotic assistance, mitigating user passivity and sustaining the engagement crucial for motor learning.

analysis.key_results: 相比仅用sEMG的基线，机器人能量消耗降低71.9%，同时保持轨迹跟踪精准；Flow State Ratio从4.6%提高到42.8%。

analysis.method: 融合EEG和sEMG的流量理论多模态协助按需控制，采用四象限模糊决策引擎生成自适应阻抗控制。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出一种基于流量理论的多模态协助按需控制框架，融合EEG心理投入和sEMG生理投入，实现上肢外骨骼的自适应阻抗控制。

papers.abstract: Mathematical agents are commonly evaluated by answer accuracy or proof acceptance. We introduce ClaimScope, a 72-task benchmark for auditing proposed claims through a verdict, scope, counterexample, and repair. Tasks cover optimizer-state transport, finite-horizon affine recurrences, and exact $2\times2$ linear algebra. We evaluate Qwen3-8B with direct generation and four matched two-pass conditions, each starting from the same draft. A witness checker evaluates only the model's submitted state, without consulting reference verdicts or supplying a replacement witness. Its feedback still conveys information about validity: a verified refutation establishes that the claim is false, and rejection reasons can suggest structural fixes. In this evaluation, verifier feedback yields $23/39$ accepted counterexamples on invalid claims and $25/72$ safe completions, compared with $15/39$ and $20/72$ for checker-free generic feedback. Strict completion remains $17/72$; verdict accuracy changes from $47/72$ to $46/72$. The claim-grouped safe-completion difference is $.094$, with a bootstrap 95\% interval of $[.000,.198]$. All seven task-level gains follow horizon/input-length diagnostics. A post-hoc schema-only correction of the direct outputs reaches the same 25 safe tasks without another model call. These results separate claim classification from executable evidence, while locating the observed gains in witness-structure correction rather than demonstrating broader reasoning improvement.

analysis.key_results: 验证器反馈在无效命题上获得23/39的接受反例和25/72的安全补全，相比之下无检查器通用反馈为15/39和20/72；严格补全仍为17/72；判决准确率从47/72变为46/72。
analysis.main_contribution: 引入ClaimScope基准，用于审计数学命题，并提供一种通过见证检查器反馈改进模型生成的方法。
analysis.method: 使用Qwen3-8B直接生成，并比较四种双阶段条件（均从同一草稿开始）下的表现，通过一个见证检查器仅评估模型提交的状态。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: 该论文提出一个用于数学命题审计的基准，并评估了验证反馈对模型生成证伪、修复和补全的影响。

papers.abstract: Specialized vision-language-action (VLA) policies acquire strong domain-specific skills, yet consolidating these skills into one shared policy remains challenging. On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers teacher knowledge on inputs induced by the student, addressing the distribution mismatch encountered during deployment. For flow-based VLAs, this mismatch arises at two levels: environment observations and intermediate action-generation states. We propose a two-level on-policy distillation framework that couples student-driven environment interaction with teacher velocity supervision along student-generated action flow trajectories. Frozen domain specialists jointly supervise one student. After each update, the student collects new environment experience and generates fresh action-flow trajectories. Starting from a joint supervised fine-tuning (SFT) initialization, Velocity Loss OPD yields absolute success-rate gains of 22.55% on LIBERO-40, 33.4% on CALVIN five-instruction sequences, and 22.6% on Meta-World MT50. Compared with Action Loss OPD and Teacher-rollout SFT, it achieves absolute success-rate gains of 6.4-9.5% on LIBERO-40, 9.7-18.3% on CALVIN, and 3.2-4.2% on Meta-World MT50. Analysis by sequence length further shows larger success-rate gains on longer CALVIN sequences. These results demonstrate effective multi-domain capability consolidation through two-level on-policy supervision, with a single student deployed across domains.

analysis.key_results: 在LIBERO-40上绝对成功率提高22.55%，在CALVIN五指令序列上提高33.4%，在Meta-World MT50上提高22.6%；相比Action Loss OPD和Teacher-rollout SFT，在LIBERO-40上提高6.4-9.5%，在CALVIN上提高9.7-18.3%，在Meta-World MT50上提高3.2-4.2%。

analysis.one_sentence_summary: 提出两级在线蒸馏框架，通过学生驱动环境交互和教师速度监督来整合多个领域专用流式VLA策略。

papers.abstract: Scaling expert demonstrations alone does not enable generalist robot policies to improve from deployment. Real-world rollouts contain successes, suboptimal behavior, and failures: imitating every recorded action can reinforce poor behavior, while filtering out failures discards evidence of physical interactions and their consequences. We introduce LoopWAM, a closed-loop world-action model that learns directly from this full quality spectrum, using rollouts from both itself and other deployed policies. Source-dependent noise sampling unifies behavior learning and action-conditioned world modeling, while quality steering and quality-weighted supervision retain full video supervision across qualities and regulate action imitation. Video and action tokens interact throughout parallel denoising, allowing learned consequences to inform action generation directly. On RoboChallenge Table30-V2, three deployment-and-training rounds raise success from 23.67% to 43.33%, a 19.7-percentage-point gain, with a final score of 56.80. LoopWAM also achieves 94.5% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 and 49.5% overall success on RoboCasa365 without additional embodied pretraining, obtaining the best overall results among the compared methods across all three benchmarks. On challenging shirt folding task, two rounds of deployment-driven improvement after single-task post-training raise success from 13.20% to 55.56%. These results demonstrate closed-loop improvement from mixed-quality experience under both multi-task learning and single-task post-training. Project page: https://loop-wam.github.io/

analysis.key_results: 在RoboChallenge Table30-V2上，三轮部署训练使成功率从23.67%提升至43.33%（提升19.7个百分点），最终得分56.80；在RoboTwin 2.0上平均成功率达94.5%；在RoboCasa365上整体成功率49.5%，在三个基准上均取得对比方法中最佳结果；在具有挑战性的叠衣任务上，单任务后训练后两轮部署改进将成功率从13.20%提升至55.56%。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出LoopWAM，一个闭环世界-动作模型，能够直接利用包含成功、次优和失败的全质量谱部署数据进行策略学习，无需过滤或仅模仿成功轨迹。
analysis.method: 源相关噪声采样统一行为学习和动作条件世界建模；质量引导和质量加权监督保持全视频监督并调节动作模仿；视频和动作令牌在并行去噪过程中交互，使学习到的后果直接指导动作生成。
analysis.one_sentence_summary: LoopWAM提出一种闭环世界-动作模型，从混合质量的部署轨迹中学习，通过质量加权和源相关噪声采样实现持续策略改进。

papers.abstract: Agentic visual generation produces experience that can improve the native understanding (agent) and generation roles of a unified multimodal backbone, but task success alone does not determine which role should learn. Generator updates can also make the agent's action supervision stale. We introduce RSIgen, a task-centric reciprocal self-improvement framework linking learning allocation, supervision refresh, and recursive curriculum construction. Dynamic Responsibility Routing (DRR) uses matched interventions on evidence, inputs, and supported actions to select learning recipients and construct compatible training targets. After generator learning, RSIgen re-evaluates the relative utility of tested actions with branch inputs held fixed to refresh agent supervision; the retained roles then construct the next curriculum. Across BAGEL, Qwen-Image, and Wan-Image-7B, RSIgen improves AgentGen-Bench Full Overall9 by 3.2--3.3 points over a three-cycle SearchGen adaptation with action costs. Wan controls support allocation gains at matched role-level training exposure, refresh gains at a matched adaptation budget, and benefits from updated curriculum sources while recipients continue learning. In blind evaluation on 200 real-user requests, pooled tie-adjusted preference scores against the same baseline reach 70.0% for task completion and 64.9% for visual quality.

analysis.key_results: 在BAGEL、Qwen-Image和Wan-Image-7B上，RSIgen在AgentGen-Bench Full Overall9上比SearchGen三周期自适应提升3.2-3.3分；在200个真实用户请求盲评中，任务完成偏好得分达70.0%，视觉质量64.9%。
analysis.main_contribution: 提出任务中心的互惠自改进框架RSIgen，动态协调视觉生成中代理与生成器角色的学习，刷新代理监督并构建递归课程，提升任务完成质量。
analysis.method: 采用动态责任路由（DRR），基于证据、输入和受支持动作的匹配干预选择学习角色并构造训练目标；在生成器学习后，固定分支输入重新评估动作效用以刷新代理监督，并构建下一轮课程。

papers.abstract: Industrial manipulation in flexible manufacturing, e.g., high-mix, low-volume (HMLV) electronics assembly, requires robot policies to adapt to changing products and production conditions. Such settings impose industrial process constraints, including product variants, moving material flows, finite execution windows, and tight geometric tolerances. However, existing evaluation frameworks do not systematically capture these constraints when assessing generalist robot policies. To address this gap, we introduce LIBERO-Industry, a novel benchmark built on the widely used robot learning benchmark LIBERO, that translates the aforementioned industrial constraints into controllable task conditions and measurable success criteria. Specifically, LIBERO-Industry comprises three classic task scenarios: Static-to-Dynamic (S2D) loading, Dynamic-to-Static (D2S) unloading, and Dynamic-to-Dynamic (D2D) transfer. The suites contain 216 tasks in total that systematically vary object geometry, conveyor speed, interaction-window duration, and geometric acceptance region size. Extensive experiments across five generalist robot policies (including vision-language-action models and world-action models) show that performance progressively degrades as industrial constraints are introduced and combined. Under a shared fine-tuning and evaluation protocol, the LIBERO-Industry co-training condition achieved higher observed target-transfer completion than the original-LIBERO condition.

papers.abstract: Physical AI requires models to ground visual and linguistic understanding in real-world environments while accounting for environmental constraints and execution feedback. We introduce MachEmbodied-VLM (ME-VLM), a unified vision-language model with two variants, 4B and 35B-A3B, that brings together embodied cognition and multimodal agent capabilities. Our work emphasizes physical perception and spatiotemporal reasoning, together with planning, interaction, and outcome assessment in both digital and physical environments. We construct training data spanning embodied and multimodal agent tasks, including execution observations and feedback to support outcome assessment and decision refinement. The training pipeline comprises embodied capability injection, separate reinforcement learning of embodied and multimodal-agent experts, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation that consolidates their complementary capabilities into a single model. Experiments show competitive performance on both embodied and agent benchmarks, as well as on autonomous-driving and embodied-navigation tasks. For edge deployment, visual token compression, W4A8 quantization, and hardware-software co-optimization enable on-device inference of the 4B variant on the M100, reducing prefill latency from 400 ms to 188 ms. Project Page: https://machembodied.com/ME-Brain/ME-VLM.html Code Repository: https://github.com/MachEmbodied/ME-VLM

papers.abstract: Vision-language-action policies are typically evaluated one perturbation at a time, providing a useful diagnosis of their sensitivity to individual distribution shifts. Real-world deployment, however, may involve several shifts simultaneously, and it remains unclear how these individual robustness measurements compose. We ask whether compound robustness can be inferred from single-axis evaluations. We introduce LIBERO-CTRL, a six-axis benchmark that pairs each initial state across single-axis conditions and a matched simultaneous condition. This design reveals two opposing outcome changes that aggregate success rates cannot distinguish: emergent failures, where all single-axis rollouts succeed but the simultaneous rollout fails, and compensated successes, where at least one single-axis rollout fails but the simultaneous rollout succeeds. Because one transition decreases compound success while the other increases it, they can cancel, making aggregate compound performance appear consistent with single-axis measurements even when individual outcomes differ substantially. These opposing transitions can largely cancel in aggregate: even when the difference between the two transition rates is not statistically distinguishable from zero, as many as 29.0% of matched initial states still change outcome. Across six policies and three severity levels, such outcome changes reach 34.5% in the most affected condition. The relative prevalence of the two transitions varies across policies and severities, while the transition rates remain similar under independent re-evaluation of stochastic policies. Compound robustness therefore cannot be characterized from aggregate single-axis success rates alone; matched per-instance evaluation is needed to reveal how joint perturbations alter behavior.

analysis.key_results: 即使单轴与复合成功率之差统计上不显著，仍有高达29.0%的匹配初始状态结果发生变化；六策略三严重度下最受影响条件达34.5%。

papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are increasingly used to make decisions for drones, but existing evaluations are mostly limited to simulation, to a single drone, and to targets that are visible from the start and do not move. We present DroneCATS, a benchmark in which the MLLM alone controls the drone through four actions, and evaluate ten MLLMs from frontier models to small open models. The benchmark varies target visibility, target motion, scene and simulator, and extends to real drones. Beyond a single drone, it adds a multi-drone suite, where one model drives multiple drones, and a commander + sub-agents suite, where a commander model directs one sub-agent for each of the drones. Across these settings, we find that frontier models achieve the highest success rates, but their latency causes them to lose moving targets, while small open models often do not declare arrival even when they reach the target. Guided by this failure analysis, we fine-tune a 2B model on drone action data synthesized from public RGB-D images; its success rate rises from 0% to 31% in simulation and outperforms the frontier models in real flight. With multiple drones, we find that every zero-shot model succeeds more often as the commander of one sub-agent per drone than when it drives all of them from one context, and that commanding success follows general VLM ability. On real drones, we observe that the results broadly follow those in simulation, while latency and hardware limits matter more. We will fully open-source the benchmark.

papers.abstract: Camera-only end-to-end (E2E) driving models are nearing deployment, where the camera stream is degraded by blur, noise, low light, weather, frame loss, and memory faults. How much a policy tolerates before its driving breaks is unclear. Corruption-robustness benchmarks target detection or bird's-eye-view perception, not the planning output that drives the car. We present DriveDegrade, a benchmark for image-degradation tolerance in camera-only E2E driving. Sixteen corruption families at five severities are injected on the fly inside the image loader, one operator reaching fifteen policies, and we evaluate open-loop planning on nuScenes and NAVSIM plus a CARLA closed-loop anchor. First, mild degradation barely affects planning, and the families that break it have a clear threshold at mid severity. Second, fragility is corruption-dependent: blur, JPEG, and raindrop damage planning most, while weather and bit error are tolerated far into the range. Third, a flat curve is ambiguous, so we separate corruptions that degrade the image from those that remove it. A planner that reads its camera must lose accuracy when information is deleted, whatever it does under quality loss. On these two axes the planners separate sharply, quantifying the ego-status shortcut without mistaking indifference for robustness. A released vision-language-action planner is flat on both axes, and blinding all six of its cameras costs it only 11.5 percent.

analysis.key_results: 轻微退化对规划影响很小；模糊、JPEG和雨滴破坏规划最严重，天气和位错误则被很好地容忍；通过区分图像质量退化和信息删除两类腐败，揭示了驾驶策略中的自我状态捷径；一个已发布的视觉-语言-动作规划器在两类腐败上都表现平坦，遮挡全部六个摄像头仅损失11.5%规划精度。

papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) used as robotic critics, reward generators, and failure detectors must understand how manipulation unfolds, not only whether it succeeds. Yet fine-grained process supervision is not readily available in a unified form, and existing evaluations do not systematically diagnose these abilities. We introduce Robo2Process, a trace-grounded framework for scalable construction of process-aware supervision from heterogeneous robotic execution data. It aligns visual observations with source-native signals and annotations, extracts local process units (LPUs), and generates structured QA supervision through task-specific sampling, deterministic label construction, and ambiguity filtering. We instantiate this framework as RoboProcessBench, a diagnostic benchmark with 12 question families spanning \emph{static monitoring} and \emph{dynamic reasoning}, and ProcessData, a corpus of 57,892 QA pairs across four data sources and 260 manipulation tasks, split into ProcessData-SFT and ProcessData-Eval. Evaluation of a broad suite of VLMs reveals uneven process understanding. Supervision from ProcessData-SFT improves \textit{Qwen2.5-VL-7B} and \textit{InternVL-3-8B} on local state, motion, progress, and primitive-aware cues. External evaluation on RoboRewardBench shows Robo2Process enables out-of-distribution process-aware reasoning abilities. Overall, Robo2Process provides a source-aware pipeline, diagnostic benchmark, and learnable substrate for process-aware understanding in robotic manipulation.

papers.abstract: While large vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly adopted as the perceptual backbone for embodied agents, their fundamental vision-language grounding (VLG) capability in embodied scenarios remains unexplored. We present \textbf{EPIC-Bench}, \textbf{E}mbodied \textbf{P}ercept\textbf{I}on Ben\textbf{C}hmark, a fine-grained grounding benchmark designed to systematically evaluate the VLG capabilities of VLMs in real-world embodied environments. EPIC-Bench comprises 6.6k meticulously human-annotated tuples (Image, Text, Mask) spanning three core stages of the embodied interaction pipeline: Target Localization, Navigation, and Manipulation. With 23 fine-grained tasks, multi-dimensional settings and evaluation over 80 leading VLMs, EPIC-Bench provides a diagnostic analysis.

papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action Models (VLAs) inherit their visual and linguistic capabilities from Vision-Language Models (VLMs), yet most VLAs are built from off-the-shelf VLMs that are not adapted to the embodied domain, limiting their downstream performance. In this work, we propose EmbodiedMidtrain to bridge the gap between VLMs and VLAs. We first characterize the data distribution gap between them, showing that VLA data occupy compact regions that are largely separated from the broader VLM distribution, while the degree of alignment varies substantially both across and within VLM data sources. Then, we build a mid-training data engine that leverages a lightweight learnable proximity estimator to select the most VLA-aligned candidates from a large VLM pool, and produce EmbodiedMidtrain-1M, a VLM dataset that we further use to mid-train the VLM before downstream VLA fine-tuning. Experiments on both simulated robot manipulation benchmarks and real-world tasks show consistent VLA performance gains over off-the-shelf checkpoints across VLM backbones and VLA action heads. These gains extend to downstream tasks not used to guide data selection. Further analysis reveals that mid-training provides a stronger initialization for VLA fine-tuning, with gains emerging from the earliest steps and widening throughout training. Moreover, the data engine captures both dataset-level and sample-level alignment signals, favoring spatial reasoning over text-centric tasks while preserving the diversity of the VLM data. We will release all code, data and models for future research.
